method.evidence: Merged WS-03, WS-04, and WS-06 outputs plus their linked primary sources were re-read. No new runtime or buyer experiment was executed in WS-12.
method.selection_rule: Choose domains for contrast rather than convenience: one favorable transfer case, one adaptation case, and one failure-heavy case.
limits: This is synthesis over bounded source sets, not proof of universality or impossibility.
External documentation is mutable and was not newly archived by WS-12.
No live control plane, security policy service, infrastructure reconciler, or migration engine was run.

strongest_transfer.statement: Cybersecurity rule-and-policy enforcement best matches the layered architecture because tested rule artifacts, separate policy bundles, and external enforcement already exist.

strongest_failure.statement: Data engineering / schema evolution shows that a machine-generated transition path is not equivalent to semantic safety, data preservation, or downstream compatibility.

verdict.thesis_statement: Generalization supports typed artifacts, authority separation, and deterministic validation, but weakens any universal passive-package or single-scan claim.

selection_reason.statement: This is the most favorable transfer case because versioned rules, policy engines, and explicit enforcement points already exist.
This domain tests whether the architecture survives long-lived control loops, side effects, provider APIs, and drift.
This domain tests whether migration graphs and validators can safely stand in for semantic correctness and data preservation.

observation.example: Scan inputs, finding locations, and logged policy inputs/results become typed artifacts.

domain_knowledge.example: Semgrep rule files encode repeatable security checks and optional fixes.

provider_knowledge.example: Rule engine version bounds and bundle verification configuration affect execution separately from rule text.

organization_policy.example: ABAC-style policy evaluation and decoupled OPA policy ownership let organizations encode local gates and exceptions.

user_intent.example: The caller can request report-only, autofix-limited, or block-on-merge behavior without changing the rule artifact.

legal_transitions.example: Report a finding, apply a narrow fix, or deny an action at an enforcement point.

agent_judgment.example: The agent can triage, explain, and draft remediation when no deterministic fix exists.

validation.example: Semgrep rule tests and OPA policy tests provide repeatable deterministic validation.

authority.example: Rule publishers do not own repository write access or deploy credentials; enforcement remains external.

mismatches.statement: Skipped incompatible rules are not the same as successful validation.
Decision logs can be masked, dropped, or rate-limited and therefore are not complete audit truth by default.

false_analogies.statement: A passed rule suite does not prove absence of exploitable behavior.

validation_profile.strength: Strong deterministic tests for rules and policies.
validation_profile.missing_assurance: Coverage completeness, exploit absence, and immutable audit completeness remain unproven.

observation.example: Desired state, current cluster state, admission request context, and provider schemas all matter.

domain_knowledge.example: Operators capture human operational knowledge while providers implement API-specific behavior.

provider_knowledge.example: Provider locks, checksums, and provider protocol behavior remain provider-specific concerns.

organization_policy.example: Admission plugins and request validation are configured by the cluster administrator, not by the workload author.

user_intent.example: Preserve availability, deploy to a chosen target, or upgrade within a maintenance window.

legal_transitions.example: Reconcile resources, mutate or reject requests, and apply provider-managed changes.

agent_judgment.example: The agent can propose rollout order or explain drift, but cannot eliminate the need for refreshed state and rebinding of approval.

validation.example: envtest covers a partial control plane; acceptance tests run real apply/refresh/destroy flows and require credentials.

authority.example: The effective authority boundary is the execution gate and credential holder, not the operator or provider author.

mismatches.statement: Operators are active control loops, not passive package lookups.
Admission handling includes side effects and reconciliation requirements, so one-shot approval is insufficient.

false_analogies.statement: A single neutral observation snapshot is not enough for a reconciler domain with drift and retries.

validation_profile.strength: There are meaningful deterministic checks, but high-confidence validation often requires live APIs, credentials, and side-effect observation.
validation_profile.missing_assurance: Static snapshots do not prove safe runtime convergence or correct production approvals.

observation.example: Current revision history, current database version, schema documents, and metadata diffs are explicit inputs.

domain_knowledge.example: Alembic revision graphs and JSON Schema vocabularies encode reusable structural knowledge.

provider_knowledge.example: SQL dialect behavior, validator configuration, and reference resolution remain engine-specific concerns.

organization_policy.example: Destructive changes, retention windows, rollback requirements, and maintenance windows remain local policy.

user_intent.example: Additive migration, backward compatibility, or an exception for a breaking change can all differ with the same starting schema.

legal_transitions.example: Generate a candidate migration, review or edit it, then apply ordered revisions.

agent_judgment.example: Rename recognition and corrective editing remain necessary because autogenerated diffs are not perfect.

validation.example: Alembic check and JSON Schema conformance tests provide structural validation.

authority.example: Database credentials and release approval still determine whether a migration runs.

mismatches.statement: Autogenerated migrations always require review and correction by hand.
Structural validation does not prove data preservation, downstream compatibility, or rollback correctness.

false_analogies.statement: A migration path that exists is not the same as a migration path that is safe.

validation_profile.strength: Revision graphs and schema validators are strong for structural correctness.
validation_profile.missing_assurance: Semantic meaning, data backfills, user-visible behavior, and recovery guarantees remain outside the narrow checks.

cross_domain_findings.statement: Typed artifacts plus independent authority plus deterministic validation transfer better than a universal package abstraction.
Domains with drift, long-lived control loops, or partial effects require repeated observation refresh and execution-time approval rebinding.
Single-scan sufficiency and validator-passed-as-safety are invalid cross-domain assumptions.
